in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with the first question: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 15 and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 15 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And the next question: **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Based on the information you've provided:

- You have a son named Alex who is 15 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you

This means you meet the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK, and you're usually considered responsible for a child if you live with them.

Just one final question to ensure there are no circumstances that might affect eligibility: **Is Alex in full-time education, and is he working for 24 hours or more per week, or claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much - just does odd jobs here and there. He's not claiming any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on all the information you've provided:
- Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- He's not claiming benefits in his own right

You meet all the standard eligibility requirements for Child Benefit.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

If you'd like to proceed with your claim, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government process. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
